plan.estimand: Minimum total development sample size for a survival prediction model meeting Riley precision and shrinkage criteria
plan.hypothesis: The prediction model will achieve adequate discrimination and calibration performance with controlled overfitting as measured by the absolute difference between apparent and adjusted Nagelkerke R-squared
assumptions: Cox-Snell R² adjusted value of 0.051 is the true model performance in the development sample
Event rate of 0.065 per person-year is constant over follow-up
Mean follow-up of 2.07 years is representative of the expected follow-up distribution
Shrinkage factor of 0.90 represents the expected calibration slope after model fitting
Prediction horizon of 2 years aligns with model performance assessment
Riley criteria are applicable to this survival prediction context
pmsampsize 1.1.3 default specifications are appropriate for the design
Nagelkerke R² scale is the appropriate performance metric for survival models in this package
missing_information: Confirmation that the Riley method via pmsampsize 1.1.3 handles survival outcomes with the specified Cox-Snell R² metric correctly
Clarification of whether the shrinkage factor 0.90 should be input directly or if pmsampsize expects a different specification
clarification_questions: Should the shrinkage factor of 0.90 be input directly to pmsampsize::pmsampsize() or is a different parametrization required?
Does pmsampsize 1.1.3 accept Cox-Snell R² or should it be converted to Nagelkerke R² for sample size calculation?
Should the verification of 'average outcome-risk absolute margin of error 0.05' be performed post-hoc using the returned sample size, or is this already incorporated into the Riley calculation?
scientific_notes: The Riley criteria are standard for prediction model development sample size determination, balancing model complexity against overfitting
With 30 candidate predictors and relatively low adjusted R² (0.051), adequate sample size is critical to avoid overfitting and shrinkage
The prediction horizon (2 years) should match the mean follow-up (2.07 years) for meaningful predictions
Shrinkage factor 0.90 implies modest expected calibration shrinkage; this is more optimistic than 0.8–0.85 common in clinical models
Verification of the outcome-risk margin of error is a secondary precision check on the predicted risk probabilities
